chords._schema: strings ordered low E (6) to high e (1). frets: null = muted/not played, 0 = open. fingers: 0 = open, 1 = index, 2 = middle, 3 = ring, 4 = pinky, null = muted.

exercises.name: Make Am

params.fingers: index(1) B 1st, middle(2) D 2nd, ring(3) G 2nd
params.open_strings: A and high-e ring open; low E muted

exercises.coaching: Am is one finger lower than A: index on the B string first fret, middle on the D second, ring on the G second. Low E quiet. Same hand position, sadder sound.

exercises.name: All six change pairs
exercises.purpose: Drill every pair among the five chords.

params.cue: one chord per 4 beats, all pairs covered

exercises.coaching: Run the six pairs: Em-C, Em-G, C-G, D-Em, Am-Em, Am-C, Am-G, Am-D. One chord per four beats. This is the full change vocabulary of beginner repertoire.

avatar_coaching_copy.intro: Am is the sad cousin of A — one finger lower, completely different feeling. With it, Em-C-G-D-Am is the set behind thousands of songs.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex1_intro: Am: index on B first fret, middle on D second, ring on G second. Low E quiet. Same little triangle as A, just dropped down a fret. Listen — it is wistful.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex2_intro: Now all six pairs, one chord per four beats. Em-C, Em-G, C-G, D-Em, and the Am pairs. This is your complete beginner change toolkit.
avatar_coaching_copy.results: Five chords, all pairwise changes fluid. You can now follow an enormous number of songs.
avatar_coaching_copy.wrap: The big set is complete: Em, C, G, D, Am. Lesson 10 we chain four of them into your first real progression.
